summary: Initial PLG-focused discovery. Haven Data is evaluating Redwood hosted API for developer self-serve, wants fast time-to-first-token and free credits to prove integration. They have medium security needs but may need Dedicated/Private for some regulated datasets. Agreement to run a quick hosted POC; Redwood to provide quickstart, creds, and benchmark template.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 38m
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Maya (CTO), Rajiv (ML Eng), Tara (Product), Leo (Infra)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for making time, um this is lena from Redwood, i'm joined by arjun on the se side and sofia from cs, quick intro round?
[00:12] Maya: maya here, CTO at Haven Data, we run a couple of internal developer platforms and looking to add LLM-powered summarization endpoints, curious about onboarding speed and costs.
[00:23] Rajiv: hi all, rajiv - i'll be doing the integration work, primary concerns latency and ability to keep some requests in our VPC later.
[00:30] Arjun: great, thanks, quick note - today's focus per the invite was PLG quickstart: self-serve hosted api, free credits, time-to-first-token, then we can talk Dedicated/Private when you have longer-term reqs.
[01:02] Lena: can i ask about current stack? where are you hosting models or do you call openai today?
[01:10] Tara: currently devs call openai for protos, and we have an internal microservice for ensembling. we'd like to move to a single endpoint for prod, ideally something our devs can use with minimal infra.
[01:28] Leo: infra-wise we run in GCP, k8s, we have a corporate VPC and we care about egress controls - for now a hosted API is fine for prototyping but we'll need VPC or private plane for regulated customer data.
[01:50] Arjun: perfect - so for a PLG quickstart you can spin up an API key, use our sdk or curl, we give free credits for a two-week trial to run initial smoke tests. Typical time-to-first-token for basic text-gen is under 5 minutes from signup assuming you have a prompt ready, it really is designed for fast dev flow.
[02:22] Rajiv: under 5 minutes - nice. question on request volume: our devs will do dev testing then some nightly batches; curious about rate limits and autoscaling.
[02:38] Lena: hosted tier has adjustable quotas and rate-limits; for higher sustained throughput you can move to Dedicated which reserves GPU pools and gives predictable throughput. For POC, we'll keep you on hosted and if you exceed quota we can provision burst capacity.
[03:05] Maya: what about cost - especially token cost vs latency trade-offs?
[03:12] Arjun: good Q - you can pick model variants, some are cheaper/quantized with slightly different latency profiles. Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles by workload; we can show you recommendations once we see sample traffic.
[03:38] Tara: is there any client-side SDK or examples? i want something our frontend devs can use fast.
[03:45] Lena: yes we have quickstarts: node/python sdk, a cURL example, and a one-click postman collection. i'll drop links in follow up (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart).
[04:02] Rajiv: security - can you describe data retention and encryption? we need SSO, audit logs, and KMS for keys.
[04:12] Arjun: hosted supports customer-managed KMS for keys in our Private offering; hosted keeps request logs for troubleshooting with configurable retention, and we provide audit logs, SOC 2 attestation, and SAML SSO integration for org-level controls. note: some of those features are gated to enterprise/dedicated tiers.
[04:42] Leo: when you say KMS in hosted - is it customer-managed or Redwood-managed?
[04:47] Arjun: for hosted it is Redwood-managed by default, but for Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM and we support VPC/connectors. I'll be clear in the doc how that maps.
[05:10] Maya: ok good. for the POC we only need to prove integration and latency for 3 endpoints: summarize, rewrite, rerank. expected throughput small but we want 99th percentile under 300ms for the summarize endpoint.
[05:28] Arjun: 300ms p99 is ambitious on hosted depending on model/sequence length - for short prompts you can get there on optimized models, but Dedicated with pinned capacity will be more predictable. We can run a benchmark to validate. I'll share a template and example runs.
[06:01] Lena: what's your timeline? when would you want to start the POC?
[06:06] Maya: asap; we have a product milestone in three weeks, so ideally POC start next week.
[06:12] Lena: great - we can do quickstart + creds this week, you can start and share results by next Wed, then we can decide on Dedicated or Private if needed.
[06:25] Tara: any gotchas on onboarding - network whitelisting, cors, etc?
[06:30] Arjun: you'll need to allow outbound to our api endpoints; for hosted it's standard https calls, no special vpn. For Private/VPC you'll have to configure peering and we assist. Some customers do a small proxy in their VPC for sensitive traffic.
[06:58] Rajiv: what's included in free credits - are embeddings included? we rely on embeddings for search.
[07:05] Lena: credits are model-agnostic but we usually recommend using them for a mix: gen, embeddings, and a couple of trace runs. we'll note the redemption steps in the email.
[07:26] Maya: demo possibility - we'd like a short walkthrough of the console and how to monitor token costs and latency.
[07:33] Sofia: we can definitely do a 20-minute demo; arjun can show the per-route dashboards and tracing.
[07:41] Arjun: yes i can demo traces and the token-level breakdown, and show how to set rollout policies and fallback models.
[08:00] Leo: any pre-reqs for the demo?
[08:04] Arjun: just create an account, i'll give a view-only link to our console demo or we can demo on our tenant.
[08:22] Tara: for the POC we might need to run a small scale load test - what tooling do you recommend?
[08:28] Arjun: we have a benchmark spreadsheet and scripts we share; i'll send them. also suggestions about batching and kv cache: for repeated prefixes you can cache kv state reduce token cost and latency.
[08:50] Rajiv: kv cache - is that automatic?
[08:53] Arjun: it's part of the runtime optimizations, for some flows we can enable prefix caching; depends on model compatibility. i'll include notes.
[09:10] Maya: compliance question - do you have SOC 2, ISO?
[09:14] Lena: yes SOC 2 Type II, and we have ISO in progress, documentation will be attached.
[09:24] Tara: legal/contract question - for dedicated/reserved capacity what does procurement look like?
[09:30] Lena: reserved capacity is typically a monthly/annual commit with an SOW; procurement generally needs a few weeks but for a POC hosted trial there's minimal paperwork.
[09:46] Arjun: one more note on model catalog - we list curated open models and verified performance; you can pin model versions for stability during rollout.
[10:00] Rajiv: pinning is important for us to avoid regressing prod.
[10:07] Lena: okay, quick recap - we'll send the quickstart guide, free credits redemption, benchmark template, and a short console demo invite. You (Maya/Rajiv) will confirm POC scope (3 endpoints) and desired SLAs.
[10:24] Maya: sounds good. can we get an estimate on costs for sustained 100 qps on summarize?
[10:31] Arjun: i'll need sample prompt lengths and model choice to give a ballpark; but i'll include a cost calc example in the spreadsheet.
[10:45] Tara: who will be our primary contact for support during POC?
[10:48] Sofia: i'll be the csm on the thread and lena will be your ae. arjun is se for technical.
[11:00] Rajiv: small nit - we've seen slight mis-labeling in other platforms where the model names got truncated, any idiosyncrasies we should watch for?
[11:06] Arjun: fair, transcripts and logs sometimes show model aliases; we'll give canonical model ids in the quickstart.
[11:20] Lena: ok last thing - any competitors you're evaluating?
[11:25] Maya: openai for dev speed, anthro- - anthropic for safety, and we're looking at Bedrock for market fit.
[11:35] Lena: noted.
[11:40] (crosstalk)
[11:45] Arjun: i'll send the benchmarking steps - typical p99 numbers on hosted for short prompts on optimized models are ~150-350ms depending on region, sequence length, and batching; Dedicated can tighten that.
[12:10] Leo: region - we're west coast, do you have regional endpoints?
[12:14] Lena: yes us-west and eu-west today, more coming.
[12:22] Tara: any early production gotchas you've seen?
[12:27] Arjun: watch for prompt tokenization differences across models and ensuring you pin model versions; also set up monitoring for quality regressions - Redwood Optimize can help automate evals against your prompt sets.
[12:50] Maya: ok thanks everyone. next steps again?
[12:56] Lena: send quickstart + creds, arjun send benchmark, sofia will coordinate demo scheduling. POC scope confirmed to be 3 endpoints.
[13:08] Maya: we'll aim to have initial integration done in a week and share metrics. thanks all.
[13:14] Lena: thanks, we'll follow up by EOD with the materials.
[13:18] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand; timestamps approximate. Links promised: quickstart guide (https://redwood.ai/quickstart), benchmark spreadsheet (link to be provided in follow-up).
